subject: environmental-science
title: Carrying Capacity and Footprints
welcome_lead: How much Earth does your lifestyle require? Measure the ecological footprint.
meta_desc: A-Level Environmental Science adventure on carrying capacity and ecological footprints.
final_note: Humanity overshoots Earth's biocapacity by ~70% — borrowing biosphere from the future.

concepts.def: Maximum population size an environment can sustain indefinitely.
Area of biologically productive land needed to support consumption (gha per person).
Productive capacity of biologically productive land/sea (gha).
When demand exceeds biocapacity, e.g., global Earth Overshoot Day in early August.
Date humanity's resource demand exceeds Earth's annual regeneration.
Population growth slowing as N approaches K: dN/dt = rN(1−N/K).

walkthroughs.body_html: Logistic curves model density-dependent constraints. Real populations overshoot K when resources are exploited beyond regeneration.
The ecological footprint converts consumption (food, energy, materials) into global hectares. World average ~2.7 gha, biocapacity ~1.6 gha.
I = P × A × T captures population, affluence and technology drivers of impact. Reducing intensity (T) is essential when P and A rise.
